messages.content: I need to put together the St. Louis convening trip for Monday, May 5, and Tuesday, May 6. I’ll be traveling alone from Dallas. Monday’s site visit is at the Grandel Theatre, 3610 Grandel Square, from 2:00 to 4:30 p.m. Tuesday starts with a funder session at Cortex, 4220 Duncan Avenue, from 9:00 to 11:00 a.m., and the closing program is at the Contemporary Art Museum, 3750 Washington Boulevard, from 4:30 to 6:00 p.m. Please compare flights, one hotel night, and the transfers. The allowance is $850 before meals.

I can build the combinations around those times. Will you check a bag, and does the $850 need to cover transportation between your home and the Dallas airport, or only airfare, the St. Louis hotel, and transportation in St. Louis?

One checked bag. Leave the Dallas-side rides out because I’ll arrange those separately. I can use either DFW or Love Field, but I need a real cushion before the Monday visit, not an arrival that works only if everything is perfect.

The three useful Monday nonstops are an American flight from DFW at 6:50 a.m., arriving STL at 8:39 a.m.; a Southwest flight from DAL at 8:10 a.m., arriving at 9:55 a.m.; and an American flight from DFW at 10:25 a.m., arriving at 12:10 p.m. Current round-trip combinations range from $219 to $286 with one checked bag included or added as applicable. The 12:10 arrival gives you only 1 hour 50 minutes before the visit, so baggage claim and a normal rideshare would consume most of the margin.
Drop the 10:25 flight. Compare the two earlier ones more carefully, including when I could reasonably reach the hotel, leave my bag, and get to the Grandel.

With the 6:50 DFW flight, a reasonable sequence is landing at 8:39, collecting the bag by about 9:05, reaching a Midtown hotel around 9:35, and arriving at the Grandel by 1:30 after lunch or work time nearby. That leaves about 2 hours 25 minutes between expected hotel arrival and the suggested 1:30 venue arrival. With the 8:10 DAL flight, estimate baggage collection by 10:20, hotel arrival around 10:50, and the same 1:30 arrival at the Grandel. That still leaves roughly 2 hours 40 minutes after reaching the hotel and more than four hours from scheduled landing to the program start.
The Love Field schedule is adequate, then. What are the hotel choices? The host hotel is supposed to be near Cortex, but I was also sent a cheaper downtown option that may be easier for Monday.

The host option is the AC Hotel St. Louis Central West End at $188.42 including tax for one night. It is about a 7-minute rideshare or roughly a 15-minute walk from Cortex, about 10 minutes by car from the Grandel, and about 12 minutes from Tuesday’s closing venue. The lower-cost option is the Fairfield Inn & Suites St. Louis Downtown at $146.76 including tax. It is about 7 minutes from the Grandel, but Tuesday morning’s ride to Cortex is closer to 15 minutes. Both quotes allow bag storage before check-in and after checkout; the rates shown can be canceled without charge through May 3.
Pair each hotel with the Love Field flight and show the whole estimate. Include every St. Louis ride we would actually need rather than just airport transportation.

The Southwest nonstop pairing is $286 round trip, with the checked bag included. With the host hotel, estimated rides are $28 from STL to the Grandel-area hotel stop, $15 from the Grandel to the hotel after Monday’s visit, $9 from the hotel to Cortex, $14 from Cortex to the closing program, and $31 from the museum to STL. That is $97 in local transportation and $571.42 total. With the Fairfield, the hotel is $146.76 and the rides are estimated at $27, $11, $18, $14, and $31, or $101 total. That package totals $533.76. Both are below the $850 allowance before meals.
The Tuesday sequence matters more than saving $37.66. Map it out from checkout through the airport, including what happens to my suitcase during the gap between the funder session and closing.

At the host hotel, you could check out around 8:20 a.m., leave the suitcase with the front desk, and depart at 8:35 for Cortex. That should put you there around 8:45, 15 minutes before the 9:00 session. After it ends at 11:00, you would have open time for meetings or lunch. Retrieve the suitcase from the hotel around 3:55, then leave by 4:05 for the museum and arrive around 4:17. The museum would need to hold the bag during the closing program; otherwise, a short-term luggage service would add both cost and travel time. After the 6:00 ending, the estimated ride to STL is 20 to 25 minutes in ordinary traffic.
I have confirmation that the museum will hold it, so no storage charge. What Tuesday returns are available?

There is an American nonstop to DFW at 7:35 p.m. for a $267 round-trip pairing with the early DFW outbound, and the Southwest nonstop to DAL departs at 8:40 p.m. as part of the $286 pairing. A United departure at 8:05 p.m. connects in Chicago and arrives after midnight, so it offers no useful advantage. The two nonstops are the practical choices.
For the 7:35 flight, are you assuming the program ends at 5:30? The posted end time is 6:00, and I cannot leave before it finishes.

You are right. Using the fixed 6:00 p.m. end, the 7:35 flight is too exposed. Even with a rideshare waiting, a 6:25 to 6:35 airport arrival would leave only 60 to 70 minutes before departure, and any program overrun or traffic delay could reduce that further. The 8:40 Southwest flight gives about an additional hour and is the only nonstop here with a reasonable post-program margin.
Then use the Southwest flights both ways. Does the outbound fare you quoted still include the checked bag and normal seat selection, or is there another charge hiding there?

The $286 round-trip quote includes one checked bag. It uses Southwest’s current standard fare conditions for this itinerary; there is no separate charge in the estimate for selecting a conventional seat, but the exact boarding and seat-assignment terms need to be verified on the final fare screen because those terms can vary by product and rollout date. No change or cancellation add-on is included.
Use the host hotel. Add a modest transportation buffer, and tell me exactly how much room remains in the allowance.

The selected planning package is $286 airfare, $188.42 for the AC Hotel, and $97 in expected St. Louis rides, totaling $571.42. Adding a $20 transportation contingency produces a complete trip estimate of $591.42 before meals. That leaves $258.58 under the $850 allowance. The contingency is not a prepaid charge; it is simply held for rideshare price variation or a small schedule adjustment.
Before you finalize the plan, give me the airport margins in plain terms and make sure Tuesday does not depend on returning to the hotel after the closing program.

Monday’s Southwest flight is scheduled to land at 9:55 a.m., 4 hours 5 minutes before the site visit. Allowing about 25 minutes for the checked bag, 25 minutes for the ride and hotel bag drop, and a 10-minute ride to the Grandel later, you can target a 1:30 p.m. venue arrival with substantial recovery time. Tuesday does not require a hotel return after the program: check out before Cortex, retrieve the suitcase before going to the museum, and leave it with the museum during the closing. If you depart the museum around 6:10, the expected STL arrival is about 6:35, roughly 2 hours 5 minutes before the 8:40 flight.
Select that combination but do not purchase anything yet. Record the flight times, hotel, transfer plan, full estimate, and the items that still have to be verified when approval comes through.

Selected but not booked: Southwest nonstop DAL-STL on Monday, May 5, departing at 8:10 a.m. and arriving at 9:55 a.m.; one night at the AC Hotel St. Louis Central West End for $188.42 including tax; and Southwest nonstop STL-DAL on Tuesday, May 6, departing at 8:40 p.m. The Tuesday plan is to check out and leave the suitcase at the hotel, ride to Cortex by 8:45 a.m., retrieve the bag before the closing program, use the museum’s confirmed bag hold, and leave directly for STL after 6:00 p.m. The planning total is $591.42: $286 airfare, $188.42 hotel, $97 estimated rides, and a $20 transportation contingency. It is $258.58 below the $850 allowance, excluding meals and Dallas-side transportation. Before purchase, verify that the flight prices and nonstop times are unchanged, one checked bag remains included, the applicable boarding and seat-assignment terms are acceptable, the hotel total still includes all mandatory taxes and fees, early bag storage is confirmed, and free cancellation remains available through May 3.
